summary.name: Hyper
summary.one_liner: Hyper is an extensible terminal emulator built on web technologies (Electron, React, Redux, xterm.js), configured via a .hyper.js file and extended with npm plugins.
use_cases: Install a customizable terminal on macOS, Windows or Linux
Theme the terminal colors, cursor and fonts
Extend the terminal with npm plugins
Write custom terminal plugins using React and Redux
summary.what_it_does:
Hyper provides installers for macOS (.app), Windows (.exe), Debian (.deb), Fedora (.rpm) and AppImage for other Linux distros, with the current version listed as v3.4.1. Users customize it through a .hyper.js config file covering fonts, colors, cursor shape, scrollback, shell and window size. Keymaps can be changed in the same file. Extensions are Node.js modules published on npm (tagged with the "hyper" keyword) that hook into the app via methods such as decorateConfig, onWindow, middleware and decorate* component methods. Plugins can be hot-reloaded with Command+R.</three_what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">open source
notable: Plugins and themes are npm packages that extend React components and Redux actions
Configuration and plugins are JavaScript files (.hyper.js) in the app directory
Uses xterm.js as the underlying terminal engine
caveats: Windows build has no 64-bit arm64 entry in the install table (listed as N/A)
Plugins affecting BrowserWindow only apply to new windows after hot-reload
Config at ~/.hyper.js is ignored if a config exists in the application directory
